title: Kensington Core
program: Housing, education, employment, museum, market, gathering
summary: A block on Jasper Street rebuilt as a core for Kensington: housing, work, education and gathering set around a shared open ground.
body: Kensington's crises compound each other — poverty, homelessness, addiction, poor mental health, housing exploitation and systemic racism are not six problems but one knot. The studio began by mapping that knot, then asking what a single piece of architecture could reasonably be expected to do about it.

The answer proposed here is a core: one block that carries the six things the neighborhood is missing — jobs and education, equal opportunity, rehabilitation, reasonable housing, fair housing practices, and comprehensive support — and puts them close enough together that using one makes the next easier to reach. The programs are deliberately interleaved rather than stacked in separate buildings.

On Jasper Street, under the elevated line, the block keeps its existing brick shells and threads new work between them. The Maker Factory holds exhibition space, hydroponic labs and workshops; the transit building becomes one long flexible room; a warehouse becomes the Foundations of Kensington Past museum; temporary residences sit above. Between them all is the Core itself — a splash pad and stepped open ground under a canopy, free to enter and belonging to no single program.
